steps.scene: You get a puncture on the motorway and stop safely on the hard shoulder. There's a spare wheel in the boot and you know how to fit it.

options.text: Wave down another driver to help
Change the wheel quickly and carefully
Get clear of the car and phone for help

question.explanation: Traffic passes the hard shoulder at 70 mph, a metre or two away. Don't try even a simple repair there.

steps.title: Breaking down on a motorway
steps.prompt: Your car is failing and you can't reach an exit or services. Put what you do in order.

items.text: Pull onto the hard shoulder and stop as far left as you can
Switch on your hazard warning lights
Get everyone out through the left-hand doors
Wait behind the barrier, well away from the traffic

steps.explanation: Left doors keep you out of the traffic. Once you're clear of the car, stay clear of it.

steps.title: Emergency phone or mobile?
steps.body: An emergency roadside phone tells the control centre exactly where you are. Arrows on the marker posts point you to the nearest one.

question.prompt: Why is an emergency roadside phone better than your mobile?

options.text: It lets the emergency services find you easily
It doesn't matter — they can always trace a mobile
It puts you through to a local garage

question.explanation: If you do use a mobile, read the location number off the nearest marker post so help can find you.

steps.scene: You're using an emergency phone beside the hard shoulder. Lorries are thundering past just a few metres away.

options.text: Away from the traffic, so it doesn't distract you
Towards your car, so you can watch it

question.explanation: Facing the traffic, you see a lorry coming and can brace for its draught, which could knock you off balance.

steps.scene: You've called for help from the hard shoulder. Recovery could take an hour, and it's cold and raining.

question.prompt: Where's the safest place to wait?

options.text: In the car with your seatbelt on — it's warmer
At the back of the car, ready to wave the truck down
Well away from the carriageway, behind the barrier

question.explanation: Vehicles do crash into cars on the hard shoulder. Being well clear of it, and of the traffic, is what keeps you safe.

steps.title: Stopped in a live lane
steps.body: Hazard lights on. Get out and well clear only if it's safe — otherwise stay in with your seatbelt on and call 999. Never stand near the car.

question.prompt: You break down and can't get onto the hard shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Stand behind the car to warn oncoming drivers
Switch on your hazard warning lights
Try to fix the fault quickly

question.explanation: Hazard lights warn traffic behind. Don't try repairs, and don't put anything on the carriageway to warn others.

steps.wrongBelief: Once your car is fixed, pull straight out and build up speed in the left-hand lane.

question.prompt: Your car's been repaired on the hard shoulder. How should you rejoin the motorway?

options.text: Pull out into the left lane, then speed up
Wait until a driver flashes you out
Build up speed on the hard shoulder, then move into a safe gap

question.explanation: Pulling out slowly into 70 mph traffic forces drivers to brake hard. Get up to speed first.

steps.repairNote: Build up speed on the hard shoulder first, then signal and merge into a safe gap. Watch for vehicles stopped ahead of you.
